content.text: : broad spectrum; fungicidal vs. Candida spp.

: fungicidal agent which inhibits squalene epoxidase, an essential enzyme in fungal sterol synthesis; produces a deficiency of ergosterol and an accumulation of squalene inside the fungal cell resulting in cell death
: HA, increased LFTs, skin rashes, GI upset, abdominal pain, taste disturbances, dyspepsia
: hepatotoxicity, permanent taste disturbances, depression, neutropenia, TTP, HUS, SJS/TEN, DRESS, erythema multiforme
) and interferes with functions of iron-dependent enzymes (catalase, peroxidases)
Fungistatic or fungicidal depending on dose
Mostly used topically d/t toxicities – tablet, cream, shampoo, foam, gel
: broad spectrum tx of systemic mycoses; may also inhibit some gram (+) bacteria & some parasites
: GI distress, itching, rash, HA, endocrine (gynecomastia, impotence, loss of libido, menstrual irregularities)

roles.drugs: Mild-moderate: topical terbinafine, naftifine, imidazoles (clotrimazole, oxiconazole, ketoconazole) or ciclopirox BID, continued 7–10 days after lesions clear (about 2–3 weeks); your table also butenafine, tolnaftate. Without testing: a 2-week trial of a topical antifungal with no steroid component (AAFP)
